nodes.title: Integral genus-two Fourier-index shift
nodes.statement: For ℓ∈V and p=(Q,R), S_{a,c,ℓ}(p)=(Q′,R′), where R′=R−2aℓ and Q′(x)=Q(x)+c(a(ℓ·x)²−(R·x)(ℓ·x)). This is a pair of a native integral quadratic form and an integral vector, for all integers a,c. Construct the new form using products of the native linear functionals x↦ℓ·x and x↦R·x, addition and integer scalar multiplication.
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Use dotProductBilin to obtain the two linear forms. Use QuadraticMap.linMulLin twice to obtain their square and product; combine them with Q using the existing Z-module operations on quadratic maps.

Pair that quadratic form with R−2aℓ. No half-integer division occurs in the native type. The BFH matrix expression follows by evaluating the associated polynomial: its symmetric cross term has coefficient −c/2.
acceptance: The output remains integral for odd mixed coefficients and arbitrary c.
Changing from j=0 to j=1 changes c from N to 1; it does not change the modulus 2a.
For c=0 the quadratic part is fixed, but the vector still changes by −2aℓ.

nodes.title: Discriminant quadratic form of a Fourier index
nodes.statement: Define Δ_{a,c}(Q,R)=4aQ−c(R·−)² as a native integral quadratic form on V. The invariant is the entire quadratic form, not its determinant. Under BFH a=m/N, c=N^(1−j), its symmetric matrix is 4aT−cRRᵀ; multiplying that matrix by N gives exactly U=4mT−N^(2−j)RRᵀ in (2.10).
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Construct (R·−) with dotProductBilin and its square with QuadraticMap.linMulLin; combine with Q by the native quadratic-map module operations.

The BFH relation U=N·matrix(Δ) is an algebraic substitution. Native integral quadratic forms are represented by half-integral symmetric matrices, by the ordered-basis expansion; the particular Δ matrix has integral entries.
acceptance: The factor is 4a, not 2a; it retains mixed coefficients of a half-integral symmetric index.
Δ is allowed to be zero, degenerate or negative on nonzero vectors.
For N≠0, equality of the BFH matrices U is equivalent to equality of the corresponding Δ forms, by cancellation and quadratic-form extensionality.

sources.match: The source uses the integral symmetric matrix U. The native quadratic-form invariant is U/N, with the level factor kept explicit; the definitions are identified through the polynomial Q(x)=xᵀTx.

uses.how: Classify exactly the integral translation orbits together with the vector residue class.

nodes.title: Discriminant invariance under an integral shift
nodes.statement: For every a,c∈Z, ℓ∈V and p, Δ_{a,c}(S_{a,c,ℓ}(p))=Δ_{a,c}(p).
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Unfold the two constructions and evaluate on x using native product-linear-form evaluation. Set r=R·x and t=ℓ·x.
Expand 4a[Q(x)+c(at²−rt)]−c(r−2at)². The cross and square terms cancel, leaving 4aQ(x)−cr². Use QuadraticMap.ext to conclude.
acceptance: The identity holds at a=0, c=0 and negative a,c; no cancellation by a is used.
For p=(0,0),a=1,c=8,ℓ=e₀ the shifted data (8x₀²,−2e₀) still have zero discriminant.
Changing only the sign of the cross term in the shift destroys the cancellation.

nodes.title: Residue invariance of the vector index
nodes.statement: For all a,c∈Z, p, ℓ and i∈{0,1}, the vector coordinate of S_{a,c,ℓ}(p) is congruent to R_i modulo 2a.
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Unfold the vector projection. The difference R_i−(R_i−2aℓ_i)=2aℓ_i is divisible by 2a.
Apply Int.modEq_iff_dvd. This argument also works at a=0, when congruence modulo zero means equality.
acceptance: At a=2, shifting R by any ℓ changes each coordinate by a multiple of 4.
At a=0 every vector index stays unchanged.
The modulus is 2m/N at both cusps, rather than 2m.

nodes.title: Recovery from a discriminant and fixed vector
nodes.statement: Assume a≠0. If p=(Q,R) and q=(Q′,R′) satisfy R=R′ and Δ_{a,c}(p)=Δ_{a,c}(q), then p=q.
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Evaluate the discriminant equality at arbitrary x with QuadraticMap.congr_fun and substitute R=R′. Cancel the identical square term by integer addition.
This leaves 4aQ(x)=4aQ′(x). Since 4a≠0 in Z, apply mul_left_cancel₀.
Use QuadraticMap.ext and equality of the vector components to conclude equality of pairs.
acceptance: At a=0, p=(0,0) and q=(x₀²,0) have equal discriminants and vectors but are different pairs.
No condition on c is needed, including c=0.
Equality of determinants of Δ is not enough: when R=0,a=1, Q=x₀² and Q′=x₁² have equal zero determinants but are different forms.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of the integral shift parameter
nodes.statement: Assume a≠0. For a fixed p, the map ℓ↦S_{a,c,ℓ}(p) is injective.
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Equality of shifted pairs implies equality of vector projections. Cancel R coordinatewise to obtain 2aℓ_i=2ak_i.
Since 2a≠0, use mul_left_cancel₀ in each coordinate and function extensionality. The quadratic component is not needed.
acceptance: For p=(0,0),a=0 all shifts give p, showing why nonzero a is required.
The result includes c=0, when only the vector part detects the shift.
For a=1, vector −2e₀ can be reached from 0 only by ℓ=e₀.

nodes.title: Classification of genus-two Fourier-index orbits
nodes.statement: Assume a≠0. For p=(Q,R) and q=(Q′,R′), there exists ℓ∈V with S_{a,c,ℓ}(p)=q if and only if Δ_{a,c}(p)=Δ_{a,c}(q) and R_i≡R′_i modulo 2a for both coordinates.
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Forward: discriminant-shift and residue-shift give the two invariants, after replacing the shifted pair by q and reversing equalities/congruences as needed.
Reverse: use Int.modEq_iff_dvd to choose t_i with R′_i−R_i=2at_i and put ℓ_i=−t_i. Then the shifted pair p₁ has vector R′.

Discriminant-shift and the assumed equality give Δ(p₁)=Δ(q). Apply recover-quadratic to p₁ and q. No analytic Fourier expansion, division in Z, or representative selection beyond the two divisibility witnesses is needed.
acceptance: Equal residues alone fail for p=(0,0),q=(x₀²,0),a=c=1.
Equal discriminants alone fail for p=(0,e₀),q=(0,−e₀),a=2,c=1: their vector residues modulo 4 differ.
At a=0,c=1, the distinct pairs (0,0) and (x₀²,0) satisfy both invariant conditions but are not shift-equivalent.
Substituting the two BFH cusp scalings gives exactly (2.10) with U=N·matrix(Δ).

nodes.title: Unique Fourier index with a prescribed residue lift
nodes.statement: Assume a≠0. Given p=(Q,R) and ν∈V with ν_i≡R_i modulo 2a, there exists exactly one integral quadratic form Q_ν such that Δ_{a,c}(Q_ν,ν)=Δ_{a,c}(p).
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Use Int.modEq_iff_dvd to choose ℓ with R−2aℓ=ν. Take Q_ν to be the quadratic component of S_{a,c,ℓ}(p).
Discriminant-shift proves the required equality. For two candidates, recover-quadratic applies because both vector components equal ν; their quadratic components are equal.
The theorem prescribes an arbitrary lift ν. It neither selects a canonical residue representative nor asserts that every arbitrary pair (Δ,ν) is represented by an integral Fourier index.
acceptance: For p=(0,0),a=1,c=8 and ν=−2e₀, the unique form is 8x₀².
For ν=R the unique form is Q.
At a=0 the pair p=(0,0),ν=0 admits every integral quadratic form and uniqueness fails.

nodes.title: Coefficient equality from shift invariance
nodes.statement: Assume a≠0. Let A be any type and B a function from the native Fourier data pairs to A. Assume explicitly B(S_{a,c,ℓ}(p))=B(p) for every ℓ,p. If p and q have equal discriminant forms and coordinatewise congruent vector indices modulo 2a, then B(p)=B(q).
hypotheses: V=Z² with its ordered coordinate basis and ordinary dot product; data are native pairs p=(Q,R), Q a Z-valued quadratic form on V and R∈V.
The integers a and c are arbitrary unless nonzero a is explicitly assumed. For BFH, a=m/N>0 and c=N for j=0 or c=1 for j=1. No positivity or nondegeneracy is imposed on Q.
proofSteps: Use orbit-classification to choose ℓ with S_{a,c,ℓ}(p)=q.
Substitute that equality into the assumed shift-invariance identity. Symmetry gives B(p)=B(q). The codomain needs no linear, topological or analytic structure.
acceptance: A constant function satisfies the premise for every codomain with a chosen value.
Taking B(p)=R₀ violates shift invariance at a≠0 and cannot be used as an actual invariant coefficient.
This lemma does not establish BFH (2.9) for the analytic coefficient B_j: that premise requires its holomorphy and contour-translation argument.

nodes.title: Siegel upper half-space of degree two
nodes.statement: H₂ is the subtype of complex symmetric 2×2 matrices Z with native positive-definite real matrix Im Z. It has the induced topology and the complex-manifold structure on the three independent symmetric coordinates. The positivity condition is strict.
proofSteps: Use the symmetric subspace of M₂(C), with coordinates (Z₂₂,Z₁₂,Z₁₁). Strict positive definiteness cuts out an open convex domain.
Use native Matrix.PosDef; identify real quadratic positivity with its finite-dimensional dot-product criterion.
acceptance: iI₂ belongs; zero imaginary part does not.
A positive imaginary part cannot excuse an asymmetric complex matrix.

uses.where: BFH §1, pp.545–546, unnumbered GSp⁺ definition and fractional-linear action
uses.how: Uses siegel upper half-space of degree two in positive genus-two symplectic similitudes: GSp₄⁺(R) consists of pairs (g,μ), g∈GL₄(R), μ∈Rˣ positive, satisfying gᵀJg=μJ for native J=[[0,−I],[I,0]]. Multiplication multiplies both components. μ is uniquely determined by g. On H₂, gZ=(AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹; CZ+D is invertible and Im(gZ)=μ(C conjugate(Z)+D)⁻ᵀ Im(Z)(CZ+D)⁻¹.

Uses siegel upper half-space of degree two in bfh genus-two theta series: For positive integer a and ν∈Z², specialize the MP.6 theta kernel to θᵃ_ν(Z,W)=Σ_{R∈Z², R≡ν mod 2a} e(Z[R]/(4a)+RᵀW). The series is normally convergent on H₂×C². Its finite residue set is (Z/(2a)Z)², of size (2a)². No rank-one Jacobi-form definition is introduced here.
